questions.question: The circumference of a circle with radius 7 cm is:
questions.rationale: C = 2πr = 2π(7) = 14π cm. (49π would be the area.)

questions.question: The area of a circle of radius 7 cm is:
An angle inscribed in a semicircle is always:
questions.rationale: Thales' theorem: any angle whose arms end at the diameter's endpoints is exactly a right angle.

questions.question: The angle at the centre standing on an arc is 80°. The angle at the rim on the same arc is:
questions.rationale: The centre angle is twice the rim angle on the same arc, so the rim angle is 80°/2 = 40°.

questions.question: Two tangents are drawn from an external point P, touching the circle at A and B with PA = 6 cm. Then PB equals:
questions.rationale: Tangents from the same external point always have equal lengths, so PB = PA = 6 cm.

questions.question: A tangent meets the radius drawn to the point of contact at an angle of:
questions.rationale: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the touch point — that is what makes it touch only once.

questions.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are:
questions.rationale: All four corners lie on one circle; each pair of opposite angles sums to 180°.

questions.question: A 120° sector occupies what fraction of the circle's area?
questions.rationale: Sector share = angle/360 = 120/360 = 1/3 of the whole circle.

questions.question: Which chord of a circle is the longest?
options: Any chord through a point 1 cm from centre
A chord perpendicular to no radius
questions.rationale: Every other chord sits off-centre; the one passing through the centre (the diameter) is longest.

questions.question: If the radius of a circle doubles, its area becomes:
questions.rationale: Area scales with r²: doubling r multiplies area by 2² = 4 (while circumference only doubles).
